sections.title: Grammar: Zero Conditional and Prepositional Phrases

content.rule: Zero Conditional (If / When + Present Simple, Present Simple / Imperative / Modal)
content.explanation: We use the zero conditional to talk about general truths, scientific facts, habits, or to give direct instructions using the imperative.
content.example: If you mix red and yellow, you get orange.

items.notes: Transcribed from the source book; teacher verification required.

content.explanation: A prepositional phrase starts with a preposition (such as after, before, behind, in, under, for) and ends with a noun or pronoun without containing a verb.
content.example: Nadine never puts her cello behind the door.

content.passage: Andy Goldsworthy is a famous British artist who works both with and in nature. He creates sculptures that are made with natural materials, such as flowers, leaves, snow, grass, and wood. To do this, he uses only his hands and simple tools. Then, instead of putting his works in a gallery, he presents them outdoors in their natural environment. Because they are in the wind, sun, and rain, the works are usually temporary. They give us a sense of connection with the natural world and the way that it changes through the seasons.

content.script:
Interviewer: Wow, Mazen! The concert was amazing! You're so talented!
Mazen: Thank you so much! I loved it, but I'm always tired after a concert!
Interviewer: I'm not surprised. You played the guitar and sang for over an hour!
Mazen: It went very quickly. But nobody knew about the problem I had before the concert!
Interviewer: A problem - what was that?
Mazen: I couldn't find my guitar! I was practicing in a different room this morning, and I put my guitar somewhere, and later I forgot where. Five minutes before the concert, my friend came into the room. She saw it behind the door. I was very lucky!
